'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir]]
**Two teachers are killed by suspected [[Islamic extremism|Islamist terrorists]] inside a school in [[Srinagar]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]]. The victims, who were members of the [[Hinduism|Hindu]] and [[Sikhism|Sikh]] minorities, are the 24th and 25th civilian victims killed by suspected terrorist groups in Kashmir this year. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/7/two-kashmir-schoolteachers-shot-dead-civilian-killings-spike (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[Islamic State – West Africa Province|ISAWP]] militants kills 87 [[Boko Haram]] fighters after raiding their camp in [[Borno State]], [[Nigeria]]. The attack is said to be a reprisal over the killing of 24 ISWAP fighters, five days ago, by Boko Haram. [https://dailypost.ng/2021/10/07/boko-haram-87-iswap-fighters-killed-in-borno/ (''Daily Post'')]
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**A bomb explodes at a religious school in [[Khost]], killing one student and injuring 17 other people. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/asiapacific/2021-10/07/c_1310230311.htm (Xinhua)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Tanzania]]n novelist [[Abdulrazak Gurnah]] wins the 2021 [[Nobel Prize in Literature]], "for his uncompromising and compassionate penetration of the effects of colonialism and the fate of the refugee". Gurnah's most renowned novel is ''[[Paradise (Gurnah novel)|Paradise]]'', set in colonial [[East Africa]] during [[World War I]]. [https://www.economist.com/books-and-arts/2021/10/07/abdulrazak-gurnah-wins-the-nobel-prize-in-literature-for-2021 (''The Economist'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economy of Venezuela]]
**The [[U.S. State Department]] confirms accusations made yesterday by Venezuelan vice president [[Delcy Rodríguez]], who blamed an alleged U.S. veto for not allowing [[Venezuela]] to receive [[IMF]] COVID-19 relief funds. The State Department says that only recognized governments can access these funds. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuela-says-imf-has-not-delivered-covid-19-funds-amid-dispute-2021-10-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Balochistan earthquake]]
**At least 24 people are killed and around 200 others injured as a 5.9 magnitude [[list of earthquakes in Pakistan|earthquake]] strikes [[Harnai]], [[Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/7/earthquake-rocks-southern-pakistan-15-dead (Al Jazeera)]
*An [[list of earthquakes in Japan|earthquake]] with a preliminary magnitude of 6.1 hits [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]], and surrounding areas, injuring 41 people and stopping train lines but without any immediate reports of severe damage. According to Japan's system, this was labeled as a "strong-5 earthquake". [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/earthquake-61-jolts-tokyo-preliminary-magnitude-estimated-61-nhk-2021-10-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
****[[India]] begins the use of [[Unmanned aerial vehicle|commercial drones]] to deliver [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s to remote areas of the country in order to increase the country's [[vaccination]] rate. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-56345591 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Indonesia]]
****The [[Indonesia]]n [[National Agency of Drug and Food Control of Indonesia|Drug and Food Control Agency]] issues an emergency use authorization for the three dose Zifivax [[ZF2001]] vaccine. [https://en.antaranews.com/news/193141/bpom-issues-eua-for-chinas-zifivax-vaccine (Antara)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****[[Malaysia]] signs an agreement with [[Merck & Co.]] to obtain 150,000 courses of the experimental drug [[Molnupiravir]] as part of a transition towards the endemic phase and "living with the COVID-19". [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/malaysia-inks-deal-to-buy-mercks-pill-to-treat-covid-19 (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Korea]], [[International aid related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[World Health Organization]] begins shipping essential COVID-19 medical supplies into [[North Korea]] via the Chinese port of [[Dalian]] and quarantine facilities in the seaport of [[Nampo]], a possible sign of easing one of the world's strictest pandemic border closures. [https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2021/10/07/1043968325/north-korea-world-health-organization-covid (NPR)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Finland]]
****[[Finland]] suspends the usage of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] for people born since 1991 due to unpublished reports of rare cardiovascular side effects such as [[myocarditis]]. [https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/575703-finland-also-limiting-moderna-vaccine-for-younger-groups?amp (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Germany]]
****The [[Standing Committee on Vaccination]] recommends [[COVID-19 vaccine]] [[booster dose]]s for people over the age of 70 and care home workers. The committee also recommends [[mRNA]]-based booster doses for people who previously received the [[Janssen COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-recommends-booster-shots-for-over-70s/a-59440188 (Deutsche Welle)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports 27,550 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of new cases this year. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-business-europe-russia-moscow-0d8dfd457c87ed1c9a1684f681bb55df (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The U.S. surpasses 44 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.kristv.com/news/coronavirus/united-states-passes-44-million-mark-for-covid-19-cases (KRIS-TV)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Taiwan–United States relations]]
**The ''[[Wall Street Journal]]'' reports a contingent of [[United States|U.S.]] [[special operations|special forces]] soldiers have been deployed in [[Taiwan]] to train [[Republic of China Armed Forces|Taiwanese forces]] amid tensions with [[China]]. The military trainers were first deployed under the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/07/taiwan-us-military-trainers-china (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Estonia]] and the [[Republic of Ireland]] announce their intentions to sign an [[OECD]]-led [[Multilateral treaty|multilateral agreement]] that would set a global [[minimum corporate tax rate]] of 15 per cent, making them the last OECD member countries to join the deal. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/business-and-tech/20211007-hold-outs-ireland-estonia-sign-up-to-global-tax-reform-deal (AFP via Radio France Internationale)]

'''Law and crime'''
*The trial against a 100-year-old former [[Schutzstaffel|SS]] [[concentration camp]] guard begins in [[Germany]]. The man is accused of collaborating in the [[murder]]s of 3,518 people at the [[Sachsenhausen concentration camp]] between 1942 and 1945, when he was employed as a standing guard in the [[watchtower]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/07/trial-begins-of-100-year-old-former-nazi-concentration-camp-guard (''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Ukraine]], [[9th Ukrainian Verkhovna Rada]]
**[[Dmytro Razumkov]], the speaker of the [[Verkhovna Rada]], the Ukrainian parliament, is dismissed following his disagreements with [[President of Ukraine|President]] [[Volodymyr Zelensky]] and his ruling [[Servant of the People (political party)|Servant of the People party]]'s stances on legislation which aimed to reduce the influence of [[Ukrainian oligarchs]]. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/speaker-razumkov-dismissed-after-disputes-with-zelensky.html (''Kyiv Post'')]
*[[Politics of Norfolk Island]]
**A political party named the Norfolk Island Party is formed to advocate for the islanders' self-determination from [[Australia]]. The party's goal is to achieve sovereignty for [[Norfolk Island]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/453103/sense-of-turmoil-prompts-birth-of-norfolk-island-party (RNZ)]
*[[Poland and the European Union]]
**The [[Polish Constitutional Tribunal]] rules that the [[Constitution of Poland]] takes precedence over [[EU laws]], directly challenging the [[primacy of European Union law]] principle, escalating tensions around the [[Polish rule-of-law crisis]] and in particular around the country's controversial [[Judiciary of Poland#Reforms of late 2010s and consequences|judicial reforms]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/07/world/europe/poland-eu-law-constitution.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.politico.eu/article/poland-european-union-constitution-justice-treaties/ (Politico)]
*[[2022 Philippine presidential election]]
**Opposition leader and Vice President [[Leni Robredo]] joins the race to replace President [[Rodrigo Duterte]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-10-07/philippine-opposition-leader-robredo-to-seek-presidency-in-2022 (Bloomberg)]
'''Sports'''
*A [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]]-backed consortium, funded through its [[sovereign wealth fund]] [[Public Investment Fund]], officially purchases [[Newcastle United F.C.]] for [[Pound sterling|£]]300 million. An agreement on its purchase was finalized upon last April, but impasses on the issue of ownership among the specific entities in the consortium prevented the deal from moving forward until recently. [https://www.espn.com/soccer/newcastle-united-engnewcastle/story/4492706/saudi-arabian-takeover-of-newcastle-nears-completion-sources (ESPN)]
